findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify that the `git diff --exit-code a475e24fc9c6edb2c52afc06677803386f45899c` byte-stability check requires a full-history clone, and either document the required `fetch-depth` for CI or make the guard script emit a clear diagnostic (and non-zero exit) when the commit is not reachable.
evidence: AC item 7: 'git diff --exit-code a475e24fc9c6edb2c52afc06677803386f45899c -- docs/adr/0021... .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor_assets/dist/editor.js exits 0'

findings.finding: The O-RAN-SC byte-stability check in AC item 7 (`git diff --exit-code a475e24fc9c6edb2c52afc06677803386f45899c -- <four files>`) requires the pinned commit SHA to be reachable in the working tree's git history. In a shallow clone (e.g. CI `actions/checkout` with default `fetch-depth: 1`), this commit may not be present, causing git to error or silently miscompare — the check could fail with a 'bad object' error unrelated to byte drift, or pass vacuously depending on git behavior. The plan does not specify that the repository must be fetched with sufficient depth, nor does it constrain this AC to run only in a full-history clone.
scenarios: CI pipeline uses `actions/checkout` with default fetch-depth:1 (shallow clone); `git diff --exit-code <SHA> -- <files>` exits non-zero with 'fatal: bad object <SHA>' rather than checking byte stability, causing a confusing unrelated failure.
A developer in a freshly created worktree with partial history runs `make lint` and sees a git error rather than a vocabulary guard error.
findings.suggested_fix: In the guard script or the Makefile target that runs this check, add: `git cat-file -e a475e24fc9c6edb2c52afc06677803386f45899c 2>/dev/null || { echo 'ERROR: base commit a475e24 not reachable — run in a full-history clone (fetch-depth: 0)'; exit 1; }` before the diff command, so the failure mode is explicit and actionable.
